correctness.rationale: For each edge, single-layer inclusion probability p=6/[n(n−1)] and adjacent-pair inclusion r=p/(n−2). Two-edge absence probabilities yield the three covariance classes q−q², b−q², c−q² with q=(1−p)^m,b=(1−2p+r)^m,c=(1−2p)^m. Since r>p², adjacent covariance is positive; disjoint covariance is negative. The proof excludes any nonzero deterministic linear edge-indicator combination by comparing all-layer-identical triangles and replacing one layer, establishing positive definiteness for n≥5,m≥2. The three eigenspaces of the Johnson graph J(n,2) have explicit λ0,λ1,λ2, and the spectral projectors give Q=Σ^−1. Expanding λ0∼18α²/n², λ1∼12α/n, λ2∼6α/n and projector entries yields both precise limits, marginal correlations, and a genuine sign reversal away from α=4/3. Independent all-edge covariance enumeration and exact inversion for n=5,m=2 and high-precision asymptotic comparisons for α=.5,1,4/3,2 corroborate each step.
residual_risks: Critical α=4/3 only has zero first-order coefficient, not an eventual finite-size sign conclusion.
Linear partial correlation is a least-squares residual statistic, not conditional independence or nonlinear causal inference.

originality.rationale: The Bernoulli random-graph superposition model and many degree, clustering, and percolation observables are prior work of Bloznelis–Leskelä and collaborators. The present precise inverse covariance of all triangle-union edge indicators, its Johnson scheme decomposition, and the adjacent-edge 4/3 full-order partial-correlation transition were not found in the complete inspected primary model paper. A related published incidence-precision result for inversion indicators uses a different distribution and does not dominate the triangle-overlay computation.
residual_risks: Search non-detection is not proof of novelty; implicit equivalences in older literature remain possible.
A broader edge-array precision theorem for random intersection/overlay graphs could implicitly contain the 4/3 threshold.

value.rationale: The contrast between always-positive marginal adjacent-edge dependence and negative full-order linear partial correlation below a sharp α=4/3 is a natural structural effect of conditioning on the entire edge array. The exact precision matrix on a canonical overlapping-community model gives a useful dependence benchmark, not merely a routine covariance diagonalization.
residual_risks: The threshold is asymptotic and model-specific; no conditional-independence or causal interpretation is claimed.

final_claim: For m≥2 independent uniformly chosen triangles on n≥5 vertices, the covariance of all union-edge indicators is positive definite, adjacent marginal edge covariance is positive and disjoint marginal covariance negative; if m/n→α>0, n times adjacent full-order linear partial correlation tends to (3α−4)/(6α), and disjoint to −2/(3α).
limitations: Fixed size-three complete triangle layers sampled independently with replacement; n≥5,m≥2.
Only linear full-order partial correlations; critical α=4/3 needs a second-order expansion to classify finite signs.
